correctness.rationale: For prime p, the kernel is row-equivalent to class convolution on SL2(Fp). For odd p, semisimple trace-fiber character sums lie in Q(ζ_(p²−1)), the ±2 exceptional coefficients lie in Z, and Φ_p is irreducible over this coefficient field. Aρ(2)=p((p+1)dim Vρ^U−dim Vρ) is nonzero: every irrep degree ≤p+1 and each maximal-degree irrep has two U-fixed vectors by the principal-series two-orbit decomposition. A hypothetically vanishing Fourier multiplier would force all trace-fiber coefficients equal, contradicted by character orthogonality or direct trivial-character fiber counting. p=2 has three explicitly nonzero central multipliers 2,−4,2. Standalone modular ranks are full for p=2,3,5,7 but are finite cross-checks only.

originality.rationale: Seven substantive published-finding corpus queries, accessible historical claims, and primary full-text comparisons did not reveal the exact universal square self-restricted SL2 prime-field invertibility statement or an established theorem implying every irreducible trace-exponential convolution multiplier is nonzero. The nearest same-variety published frame uses only 4p−3 first-coordinate columns; Li–Hu evaluate aggregate ambient Fourier sums without proving the complete central-convolution nonvanishing. The statement remains subject to bounded-priority risk and is not independently certified.
residual_risks: An older complete finite-special-linear character table may implicitly make this result a corollary; no exhaustive historical priority certification was undertaken.
The author-hosted 1992 computational paper was inspected, but not every citation and earlier monograph was recursively examined.
Search-based absence cannot establish global novelty; an independent mathematical audit remains unperformed.

value.rationale: A natural critically sampled square Fourier operator on a nonlinear determinant-one variety is shown to recover every complex signal for every prime field order. The proof reduces the full matrix problem to a structural finite-group character criterion and resolves all irreducible sectors, rather than an arbitrary finite census. This supports a natural reconstruction application even without explicit spectral stability or higher-dimensional extensions.
